subject: Discovery recap + procurement next steps \u0014 Redwood x Acme Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-01T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps  Redwood x Acme Enterprise

Hi Samantha / Tom 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so were aligned and can move this toward procurement:

Key pain points you shared
- High tail-latency on customer-facing chat that spikes during peak / month-end usage and causes degraded UX.
- Cost per active session is unpredictable due to lack of batching and cache reuse; impacting unit economics for new features.
- Internal security/compliance requirement for audit logs, KMS integration, and data residency controls.

Current stack / constraints
- Frontend: customer chat on React; backend calls to an internal service that proxies requests to a third-party LLM vendor.
- On-prem data retention requirements for PII-containing logs (EU team).
- Procurement prefers an annual commitment for price predictability, with a standard Master Services Agreement.

Success criteria (what success looks like in 90 days)
1) 30% reduction in median token cost through batching/cache for the chat workload.
2) P95 latency under 600ms for the 90th percentile of active sessions.
3) Completed security review (SOC2 evidence + answers) and KMS integration plan.

Immediate next steps / procurement framing
- Well put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes stakeholders, milestones, and artifacts required for procurement and security.
- Initial commercial guardrails: we recommend two options to discuss with procurement  a Reserved (Dedicated) capacity commitment (monthly/annual) for predictable unit costs, or a Pay-as-you-go hosted plan with volume discounts past a monthly threshold. Ballpark pricing range for sizing conversation: $40k$120k/month depending on commit level and SLA. We can surface modeled estimates in the MAP.
- Decision process & stakeholders you mentioned: Steering committee (Product + Eng), Procurement (Tom), Security (internal compliance team). Typical procurement timeline you mentioned: 48 weeks after technical review.

Attachments Im sharing now:
- Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx (our answers template  Rafael will lead technical responses)
- SOW_draft_v1.pdf (initial SOW outline and options)

Proposed next meetings:
- Technical deep-dive (Rafael + Vivek from our side)  60 minutes to walk integration and SOC2 evidence  dates: Wed 5/6 or Thu 5/7 afternoon PT.
- Procurement/Commercial sync  30 minutes with Tom + procurement to align on preferred contract vehicle and PO terms.

Would you prefer we create a single MAP doc (we draft, you iterate), or would you rather run an internal RFx first and we respond? Either works  well adapt.

Thanks  looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement next steps  Redwood x Acme Enterprise

Thanks Marissa  solid recap, appreciate the clarity. A few quick notes: 

- Confirmed: decision will go to the steering committee (Product + Eng) the week of 5/18.
- Procurement lead: Tom (ccd)  hell own PO/contracting and vendor onboarding.
- Security review: our InfoSec will want the completed questionnaire + SOC2 reports. Can we target 10 business days for the initial questionnaire response?
- Budget: rough internal guardrail is $75k$100k/month for next fiscal planning; open to seeing the model for reserved vs hosted.

For process, we typically run a short RFx (vendor questionnaire) then a commercial call with procurement. I attached our Acme vendor form (Acme_vendor_form.docx)  procurement will need that back.

Lets tentatively schedule the technical deep-dive for Thu 5/7 10:00am PT  is that ok for Rafael/Vivek?

Samantha
Director, Product  Acme Enterprise
Samantha.Lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + procurement next steps  Redwood x Acme Enterprise

Thanks Samantha  Thu 5/7 10:00am PT works for our team. Rafael and Vivek will cover the technical and security topics.

A couple follow-ups before the call so we can make it productive:
- Rafael: Ive attached the Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx  Rafael, can you own the initial pass and aim to return answers within 5 business days so InfoSec has something to review before the call?
- Vivek: can prepare a short slide (34 mins) on integration patterns (KMS options, data residency, KV/prefix caching) and expected timeline for a minimal integration.
- Commercial guardrails (for procurement):
  - Option A  Reserved Dedicated: annual commitment, 2030% discount vs hosted at scale, SLA-backed latency targets, dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
  - Option B  Hosted + Volume: lower up-front, volume tiers with step discounts; recommended for teams that want to start quickly and convert to Reserved later.
  - Typical procurement asks we can support: standard MSA + SOW, PO terms NET30 (or NET45 on request), and a single annual invoice for reserved deals.

If helpful, I can draft a 1-page MAP with milestones (tech review, procurement review, contract, pilot) and a proposed timeline that you can share with your steering committee. Ill drop a HubSpot link to the deal for your procurement reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Next steps: Rafael to return the questionnaire (5 business days), Vivek to prepare integration notes, Marissa to draft MAP and SOW options.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa 

Procurement here. Confirming timeline: once we receive the filled vendor form + SOW draft and SOC2 evidence, we can target a procurement review week of 5/18 with an expected PO issuance by 6/01 pending steering committee approval.

Please send SOW_draft_v1.pdf and completed Acme_vendor_form.docx to procurement@acme.com. Our standard contract requests are NET30 payment, and a clause around data residency and audit rights; well flag any required redlines during legal review.

Thanks,
Acme Procurement Team
